# identity-callers (C++) — why there is no compile_commands.json here

clangd needs a compile database. Without one it has no index, `w.render()` resolves to an External
stub, and the caller sets are EMPTY — which for a long time was recorded as "caller attribution is
structurally unavailable", a statement about the system rather than about this fixture.

Measured with a generated compile DB (clangd 22.1.6):

| | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| records imported | 0 | 12 |
| CALLS edges created | 0 | 2 |
| `alpha::Widget::render` callers | (empty) | `alphaCaller` |
| `beta::Widget::render` callers | (empty) | `betaCaller` |

⛔ **THE SAME ROOT CAUSE AS `identity-callers-js`.** That fixture shipped with no
package.json/tsconfig.json and produced 0 edges for the same reason. Two fixtures, one failure: the
missing PROJECT CONFIG made the feature look impossible.

⚠ **The DB is generated by the test, not committed.** Its `directory`/`file` entries are absolute
paths, so a tracked copy would be wrong on every other machine. See
`tests/integration/m1-cpp-caller-sets.test.js`, which writes one into a temp copy with
`-nostdinc++` — this fixture includes nothing from the system, and a missing include path is enough
to make a TU fail to compile while background indexing still reports idle.
